prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the layout of an indoor retail space with a clothing rack in the immediate foreground (bright white/light grey, ~0.3–1.2 m away), a large multi-paned window wall running diagonally from the close left (~1.5 m) to the far center-right (~3–4 m), and a back corner wall (~4–5 m away). In frames 1–4, the clothing rack and hung garments sit below and directly in front of the camera wearer within arm's reach (~0.3–0.8 m, peaking in brightness in frame 2 when the wearer's hands lift a grey jacket on a hanger at ~0.3 m), while a bearded man stands behind the far end of the rack (~2.0–3.0 m from the wearer and ~0.5–1.0 m beyond the rack's far end) facing right and downward away from the camera wearer, with his lower body occluded by the rack. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer shifts and turns leftward past the rack until the rack moves completely out of view in frame 5, leaving the man visible from the chest up in the lower right at ~2.5 m as he turns his head slightly toward the camera wearer. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground rack and held hanger from the mid-ground window mullions and background wall while treating the transparent window glass as a continuous planar surface rather than confusing it with the outdoor parking lot and trees beyond. However, the map is unreliable in absolute scale continuity across frames—normalization shifts cause the window wall to appear much brighter (nearer) in frames 4–5 when the close foreground clothing leaves the frame, and the man's head nearly merges into the dark background depth in frames 1, 2, and 4.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the visible upper body of the bearded man (`person`) standing in the mid-ground (~2.0–3.0 m from the camera wearer, positioned to the right of the window wall and behind the far end of the foreground clothing rack), where his torso and legs are heavily occluded by the rack and garments in frames 1–4 and cropped by the bottom frame edge in frame 5. In frame 2, it also segments the camera wearer's own hands and the grey jacket held on a hanger within immediate arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m in the lower center foreground), and across the sequence it tracks the distant man shifting from the center-right (frames 1–4, facing right/downward away from the wearer while reaching within arm's reach of the far end of the rack in frame 4) to the lower right in frame 5 as he turns toward the camera wearer. While the masks sharpen the exact visible silhouette of the man's unoccluded head and torso against the cluttered rack and window background in frames 4 and 5, the map provides almost no layout information because the window wall, ceiling, and background walls are completely unsegmented black void. Furthermore, the segmentation is highly unreliable on the foreground objects within the wearer's reach: it merges the wearer's hands and the held jacket into a single `person` mask in frame 2, hallucinates two `motorcycle` instances on the clothing rack bar and hung shirts (~0.5–1.0 m away) in frame 3, and misses the rack entirely in frames 1, 4, and 5.
descriptions.pose: The body/hand skeleton map places a single yellow body skeleton on the bearded man in the mid-ground (~2.0–3.0 m in front of and slightly right of the camera wearer, ~0.5–1.0 m behind the far end of the clothing rack), with head keypoints clustered at the top and shoulder/torso/limb lines extending downward below him. From the arrangement of facial and shoulder keypoints, the man faces right and tilts his head downward away from the camera wearer in frames 1–4 (with his arms angled forward within arm's reach of the far end of the rack and counter area, especially in frame 4), before rotating his torso and head leftward to face more toward the camera wearer in frame 5 as the wearer moves past the rack. Unlike the RGB strip, where the man's lower body is completely occluded by the foreground clothing rack in frames 1–4 and out of frame in frame 5, the pose map attempts to localize his occluded hips, knees, and ankles behind the rack to indicate his full standing posture and orientation. However, these hallucinated lower-body keypoints are spatially unreliable—producing floating or anatomically compressed leg and hip geometries in frames 1–3, collapsing his torso into a narrow vertical sliver in frame 4, and misplacing an arm/hand cluster in frame 5—and the map completely fails to detect the magenta hand skeletons for either the man's hands or the camera wearer's own hands holding the hanger at ~0.3 m in frame 2.
